##Part A — Creating Vectors and List
```{r}
## Question #1:
## Create a vector for the worker’s age.
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
ages
## How many data points?
length(ages)
## Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.
min(ages)
max(ages)
## Access the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.
ages[c(13:18, 33:35)]
## Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included.
ages[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]
## Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.
ages[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
ages
```
```{r}
## Question #2:
# Get the summary statistical values of

data(rivers)
length(rivers)
sum(rivers)
mean(rivers)
median(rivers)
var(rivers)
sd(rivers)
min(rivers)
max(rivers)
# What is the result? Combine into a single vector.
results <- c(
  length = length(rivers),
  sum = sum(rivers),
  mean = mean(rivers),
  median = median(rivers),
  var = var(rivers),
  sd = sd(rivers),
  min = min(rivers),
  max = max(rivers)
)

results
```
